Syllabus

Room 63 Library. Advanced Placement Capstone, 2026-27.

Eleven books stand on the shelf in three groups. Each one opens to its own pages. Your name and period carry from the card on the cabinet into every book on this device.

  1. 1. The Research Log. Every course. The log in your notebook: its six lines, its sources, and how it is checked.
  2. 2. The Research Manual. Every course. Where sources live, how to get in, and how to use what you find.
  3. 3. The AI Manual. Every course. The College Board's AI rule and Room 63's: allowed uses, better prompts, checked answers.
  4. 4. The Field Guide to Research Questions. Every course. Finding a question of your own: the eight lenses, the anatomy of a question, six broken shapes.
  5. 5. Presenting and Defending. Every course. Your talk in seven steps: the spine before the slides, three timed runs, the defense.
  6. R1. The Proposal. AP Research. From a question to a signed form: the four families of study, your data, your needs, peer review.
  7. R2. Writing the Paper. AP Research. How research becomes a paper: question, method, argument, sources, clear prose.
  8. R3. The Process and Reflection Portfolio. AP Research. The record of the year: two kinds of pages, seven things to cover, the feedback table.
  9. S1. The Team Project. AP Seminar. The team project: how teams form, one issue and many lenses, the report, the presentation, the defense.
  10. S2. The Individual Project. AP Seminar. Your own argument from the packet: the stimulus texts, your question, the written argument, the presentation, the defense.
  11. S3. The End-of-Course Exam. AP Seminar. The exam in May: the parts, the timing, what each question asks, how it is scored, how to practice.

Books 1 to 5 are for every course. The R books are for AP Research, periods 1, 3 and 4. The S books are for AP Seminar, periods 2, 5, 6, 7 and 8. Begin with book 1 and keep the log from the first week.
